headline: AI WROTE 948
LINUX **EXPLOITS**
cover.hook_pick_reason: The 948 figure is the hardest number in the story and slide 2 backs it directly (948 working exploits out of 1,724 reproduced Linux kernel flaws, against 166 for the older model). It also raises the stakes without promising a verdict. The 'not for you' option is accurate (access is vetted) but vague on the payload; the Firefox option is true but smaller; the 'Critical' option leans on a rating label. No reader-impact hook: the articles state no direct effect on ordinary readers (price, access or risk); the only reader-level link is that fixes reached Linux and Firefox, and the model itself is limited to vetted defenders.

slides.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber
body: OpenAI announced **GPT-6 Cyber** on Nov 5, built on GPT-6 Astra. It finds software flaws, writes exploit code (programs that abuse a flaw) and runs penetration tests, or authorized mock attacks. It is not open to the public.

slides.title: 948 working exploits
body: Researchers reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities. GPT-6 Cyber wrote working privilege-escalation exploits, which give an attacker higher access, for **948**. GPT-5.6 Sol managed **166** in the same setup.

slides.title: 81 new Firefox bugs
body: It found **81** new high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox, the browser made by Mozilla, which fixed many. Per Reuters, as cited by AI타임스, 588 of the 948 Linux flaws were previously unknown.

slides.title: Rated Critical, access limited
body: OpenAI rates its cyber capability **Critical**, the highest level in its own safety evaluation, up from High for GPT-5.6 Cyber. Only approved customers of Daybreak Red, OpenAI's program for vetted security defenders, get it, after identity and permission checks.

slides.title: Not best at everything
body: On FrontierCyber, GPT-6 Cyber solved **90** of 288 tasks, below GPT-6 Astra's 96. On ExploitGym it scored **48.5%** against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

slides.title: One bug, two hours
body: Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used GPT-5.6 Sol through Daybreak Blue to find a severe Ubuntu and Debian flaw in two hours. Debian patched it; no exploitation is known. OpenAI's goal: **dramatically expand** Daybreak. Wider GPT-6 Cyber access is planned within weeks.

facts.text: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber on Nov 5 (US time); it is built on GPT-6 Astra and specialised in finding vulnerabilities, writing exploit code and penetration testing.
Researchers reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and wrote working privilege-escalation exploits for 948; GPT-5.6 Sol succeeded on 166 in the same setup.
According to Reuters (as cited by AI타임스), 588 of the 948 were previously unknown flaws.
It found 81 new high-severity vulnerabilities in Mozilla's Firefox; Mozilla fixed many.
On ExploitGym it scored 48.5% vs 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber; it did worse than GPT-6 Astra on FrontierCyber (90 of 288 tasks vs 96).
OpenAI rates its cyber capability 'Critical', the highest level in OpenAI's own safety evaluation, up from 'High' for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

Access is limited to approved customers of Daybreak Red, with identity and permission checks. Per AI타임스, OpenAI plans to widen GPT-6 Cyber to all approved customers over the coming weeks and add a group for critical infrastructure defenders.
Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used GPT-5.6 Sol via OpenAI's Daybreak Blue program to find a severe Ubuntu/Debian flaw in two hours; Debian patched it and there is no known exploitation.
OpenAI says it wants to 'dramatically expand Daybreak' to organisations of every size, independent researchers and open-source maintainers (no timeline given in this article).

sources.title_en: OpenAI launches 'GPT-6 Cyber'... exploit success rate up 51%

caption:
OpenAI's new GPT-6 Cyber wrote working Linux exploits for 948 flaws, and it is released only to vetted defenders.

OpenAI rates the model's cyber capability "Critical", the highest level in its own safety evaluation. Access runs through Daybreak, its program for approved security teams.

→ 1,724 Linux kernel flaws reproduced; 948 got working exploits (GPT-5.6 Sol: 166)
→ 81 new high-severity bugs found in Firefox, many already fixed
→ Not best at everything: 90 of 288 on FrontierCyber, below GPT-6 Astra's 96

Should a model this capable ever be released, even to vetted users?

Source: TechCrunch, "OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?", Nov 5, 2026; AI타임스 (in Korean), "OpenAI launches 'GPT-6 Cyber'... exploit success rate up 51%", Nov 6, 2026.
